Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

indri 0.4.0

Genotype-by-environment scans, environment-specific genetic covariance (experimental), a WOMBAT engine, four vignettes on the LG/SM F3 mice.

  • A fourth block engine, "wombat", runs Karin Meyer’s WOMBAT REML program (Linux and Windows, free for academic use) on each subset. It matches the sommer engine on G, E, standard errors and vcov to about 1e-5, takes covariates and gaps in Y, and holds residual covariances between traits that no individual has together (character states in fit_G_env()) at zero instead of estimating them. Point indri at the binary with options(indri.wombat = <path>), engine_args = list(wombat = <path>) or the PATH. engine_args = list(wombat_rank = q) fits G at reduced rank (WOMBAT’s principal-component analysis), for blocks whose full-rank estimate sits on the positive-definite boundary.

  • fit_G_env() fits trait-paired subsets by default: one block per pair of traits, holding both traits in every environment. With fit_G()’s usual subsets most blocks held a trait in one environment only, and the projection onto a positive semi-definite G pulled the cross-environment covariances towards zero. In simulations (10 and 30 traits) the mean cross-sex genetic correlation rose from 0.67-0.77 to 0.84-0.85 for a true 1 and from 0.38-0.45 to 0.49-0.50 for a true 0.5, with half the blocks. Pass subsets, s or min_cooccurrence for the old design.

  • The LG/SM data sets cite their source: Melo, Marroig and Wolf (2019), Journal of Heredity 110, 479-493, doi:10.1093/jhered/esz011.

  • Four vignettes on the growth traits of the LG/SM F3 mice: G estimation with the three engines and the choice of LKJ prior, genome scans for additive and dominance effects, G from locus effects, and genotype-by-sex scans. They are precomputed (vignettes/*.Rmd.orig, vignettes/precompute.R).

  • lgsm_f3 has all nine weekly gains (growth12 to growth910, the growth class of lgsm_traits); the original analyses used the first seven.

  • fit_G_env() (experimental) estimates the genetic covariance of traits within and between the groups of a discrete environment (sex, diet, site), fitting each trait in each environment as its own “character state” with fit_G() (sommer by default). G holds the within-environment blocks and the genetic covariance between environments (corr_between: each trait’s cross-environment genetic correlation); E is block diagonal, as no individual is observed in two environments. The first step towards modelling polygenic GxE in the association scans: pass the result to indri_gwas() as fit and the scan uses an environment-specific background covariance (each pair of individuals’ genetic covariance depends on both their environments). The scan rotates by a generalized eigendecomposition per connected component of A, so it stays fast for family data; it matches a dense GLS, and reduces to the usual scan when the background has no GxE. With it, the interaction tests are no longer inflated by polygenic GxE, but they are conservative: fit_G_env() underestimates cross-environment genetic correlations (0.67-0.77 for a true 1 in simulations).

  • indri_gwas(gxe = ) fits genotype-by-environment interactions: each SNP’s dosage also enters multiplied by the named columns of X (sex, diet, a covariate), whose main effects are in the model already. pvalues is the joint test of the SNP’s main effect and interactions, pvalues_gxe the interactions given the main effect, with the interaction effects in gxe (SNPs by traits by environments). Works for multi- and single-trait scans, LMM or LM, with dominance (as a main effect) and permutations; SNPs whose interactions cannot be estimated keep the main-effect test (gxe_estimable). plot(scan, which = "gxe") draws the interaction tests. GxE in the background covariance is not modelled.

  • indri_locus_G() builds the additive (G) and dominance (D) covariance matrices implied by per-locus additive and dominance effects, allele frequencies and linkage disequilibrium (Melo, Marroig and Wolf 2019, Eqs. 7-14). It takes indri_gwas()’s a and d directly, with frequencies and composite LD from the genotypes, or effects from other software: a data frame with a column of locus names, traits in rows or in columns (traits_in), loci matched to the genotypes (and to d, p, lambda) by name, and errors for 0/1/2 codings and transposed effects. The help page sets out the effect-allele, dominance and unit conventions the effects must follow.

indri 0.3.0

Association scans, the residual covariance, and data from an LG/SM intercross. fit$E is new; see below for how it is computed.

New features

  • indri_gwas() runs genome-wide association scans with the covariances indri estimates: one multi-trait “any effect” test per SNP across all the traits, or one test per SNP and trait, in a linear mixed model with the relationship matrix A or in a linear model. The covariance is diagonalised once, so a scan costs one N x N rotation of the genotypes plus O(N P) per SNP. Every test is a likelihood ratio with the overall scale profiled.
    • The multi-trait mixed model uses G and E as the shape of the covariance and re-fits one ratio delta between them by REML under the null, so the test stays calibrated if they are off in scale. delta is returned (near 1 when G and E describe the data) and can be fixed with delta =.
    • Single-trait mixed models fit each trait’s variance ratio by REML, or take it from the fit with single_trait_variance = "fit".
    • The multi-trait linear model uses the residual covariance of Y after X.
    • dominance = TRUE adds a heterozygote indicator for each SNP: pvalues becomes the joint additive + dominance test, pvalues_dominance tests dominance given the additive effect, and a and d hold the two effects. SNPs seen in only two genotype classes keep the additive test (dominance_estimable).
    • adjust = "bonferroni" or "effective" corrects single-trait p-values for the number of traits.
    • Samples are matched by row name across Y, genotypes, A and X; missing genotypes are mean-imputed; monomorphic SNPs get NA.
    • n_permutations reruns the scan with permuted genotypes: pvalues_empirical, and qvalues_empirical, a permutation estimate of the false discovery rate; fdr gives the p-value threshold at that rate (fdr_threshold). LiMMBo’s “empirical FDR” was the fdr-quantile of the permuted p-values, an uncorrected threshold; indri estimates the FDR.
    • print(), summary() (top SNPs, genomic inflation), as.data.frame(), and ggplot2 Manhattan and QQ plots (plot()); snp_info carries SNP positions into the results.
    • Checked against dense GLS and against LiMMBo’s results on its own test data.
  • indri_effective_tests() gives Galwey’s (2009) effective number of independent traits, from the residuals after X when a design is given.
  • fit_G() returns E, the residual covariance in the units of Y: the covariance of the residuals of Y on X minus the assembled G (scaled for the relatedness in A), with eigenvalues floored at 1e-3 of the largest. E_bar is the average of the block residual covariances. The block average is not used for E: at 30 traits it was strongly indefinite, its projection had eigenvalues near zero, and the multi-trait test ran at 66 times its nominal rate at 1e-4. Fits made by earlier versions have no E and cannot drive the multi-trait scan.
  • examples/gwas.R runs the whole pipeline on simulated sibs in seconds.
  • Data from an F3 intercross of the LG/J and SM/J mouse strains: lgsm_f3 (1611 mice with pedigree, rearing, and four trait classes: weekly weight gains, raw weekly weights, mandible areas and necropsy weights; lgsm_traits lists them), lgsm_genotypes (353 markers in the additive, dominance and imprinting design, for the F3 mice and their F2 parents), lgsm_markers (the map), lgsm_pedigree and lgsm_A (the F3 relationship matrix, with the F2 parents as unrelated founders: the P strains are inbred and the F1 all heterozygous). The four sires missing in the source were inferred from the markers by Mendelian exclusion (sire_inferred). Provenance still to be documented.

indri 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • G, G_bar, G_draws and sigma_G are returned in the units of Y. Fits saved by 0.1.0 hold a standardised G.

New features

  • The REML engines (sommer, asreml) report uncertainty: normal draws from each block’s sampling covariance, assembled like stanimal’s posterior draws.
  • spread = "mixture" is the default way to assemble draws, and corrG_draws mixes each block’s own correlation draws. Averaging the block draws had covered the true correlations 40% of the time at nominal 95%; the mixture brought that to nominal.
  • Non-converged REML blocks are reported in fit$diagnostics instead of trusting a single convergence flag.
  • REML engines take starting values and fit single-trait blocks.
  • stanimal blocks share one eigendecomposition of A (needs stanimal >= 0.8.0).

Defaults

  • Subsets of up to four traits (s = 3) for every engine; each pair in 3 distinct blocks for stanimal and in at least 1 for the REML engines.
  • The stanimal engine fits blocks with lkj_prior = 1.
  • asreml runs two workers by default (one licence seat each).

Bug fixes

  • sommer returned blocks in alphabetical trait order, which put variances and covariances on the wrong traits; blocks now follow the columns of Y.

indri 0.1.0

  • First version: trait subsets with guaranteed pair coverage (indri_subsets()), block assembly (indri_assemble(), indri_assemble_draws()), a least-squares projection onto the PSD cone (indri_project_psd()), pluggable block engines (stanimal, sommer, asreml) and fit_G().
